speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) why has the Government decided to allow applications for licensed public personal mobility device (PMD)-sharing services from January 2019; and (b) whether the Government will consider delaying the introduction of such commercial shared public PMD services until the riding culture for PMDs has improved and incidences of unsafe and inconsiderate usage have subsided.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: However, it is important that operators provide such services without causing public disamenities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This will limit the impact of their operations and allow LTA to assess the operators' operations and ability to comply with regulatory requirements before LTA considers granting any full licences for large-scale operations in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The safe use of PMDs is a shared responsibility between users, operators and the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: LTA is strengthening public education and enforcement for all PMD users.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This will facilitate enforcement and deter reckless riding.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: To ensure a smooth transition, LTA will engage the user community and will give a transition period for users to comply.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I think Members of the House will agree with me that it is hard enough currently to ensure that all owners of PMDs adhere to the rules for safe use of PMDs and to be considerate to the other footpath users.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And earlier this year, a lot of us spoke about this issue at the Committee of Supply debate.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I believe we are not out of the woods yet.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Would it not exacerbate the present situation if we have a new category of users, namely, hirers?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Hirers may even take less ownership of the need to ride responsibly and considerately since they are not the owners.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: My second supplementary question is: how does the Ministry of Transport (MOT) intend to educate this new group of users, the hirers?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: My next supplementary question is: what would be the responsibility of commercial-shared PMD service providers in ensuring that their hirers use their PMDs in a safe, responsible manner?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And, finally, as the Senior Minister of State has shared about the limited sandbox size, could he share with the House what is this sandbox size expected to be when this shared service is being introduced?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Yes, we had quite a comprehensive debate many months ago on the issue of bike sharing as well as the use of PMDs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With regard to the PMD-sharing services regulatory framework, there are several key considerations that LTA will take into account when promulgating that in 2019.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: One is that we will take into account recent experiences from licensing the bike-sharing operators, that is, looking into ways to prevent indiscriminate parking and the abandonment of shared PMDs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In addition to that, there are also some issues that are very specific to PMDs, like fire risks, charging issues as well as like third-party liability insurance.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA has been making an effort to ensure that PMD use as well as bike-sharing remains safe in the community.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We adopt a multi-pronged approach, one of which is public education where we work closely with the various operators to educate users on safe and responsible riding.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA also has broad-based measures to improve active mobility safety.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I think Mr Dennis Tan is also quite familiar with these, one of which includes the registration of e-scooters which will be implemented in early 2019.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Last but not least, of course, will be infrastructural improvement.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will be building more dedicated cycling paths as well as widening footpaths at locations where there is high pedestrian and cyclist volume.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Ultimately, PMDs offer a very convenient mode of commuting around Singapore and they are integral to our transport network and provide us with a car-lite alternative, especially for short distance trips.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I believe, with time, we will be able to see significant improvements to users' behaviour as well as indiscriminate parking.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With regard to the sandbox licences, more announcements will be made when we are ready.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
